No `pagy_nav` or `series`. | | `test/controllers/notes_controller_test.rb:46-95` | Tests for paging with filters, `per_page`, invalid pages, the cap at 50, and overflow to the last page | | Docs | `ARCHITECTURE.md:17-23`, `docs/guides/controllers.md:108-110` mention "Pagy 8.6.3" | None of the following use Pagy: jobs, mailers, models, `lib`, `config/locales/en.yml` (no `pagy.*` keys), importmap or `vendor/javascript` (no pagy.js), jbuilder, response headers, metadata, keyset, calendar, or countless pagination. Rename the extra in the initializer** (`config/initializers/pagy.rb`) - **Why:** 9.0.0 renamed `items` to `limit` (changelog "Simple renaming" table). `pagy/extras/items.rb` no longer exists. - **When it applies:** always. On 9.3.5 boot fails with `LoadError: cannot load such file -- pagy/extras/items` (variant A). Sidekiq workers boot the same Rails app, so they would fail to start too. - **Hidden trap:** fixing only the `require` line boots fine. But the old keys are then ignored, so you silently get 20 per page, a `limit` URL parameter in place of `per_page`, and a cap of 100. - **Change:** `require "pagy/extras/limit"`, `DEFAULT[:limit] = 10`, `DEFAULT[:limit_param] = :per_page`, `DEFAULT[:limit_max] = 50`. Keep `:overflow = :last_page` and the comments. - **Keep `:per_page` as the parameter name.** Switching to the new default `limit` would break bookmarked and shared URLs. - **Works on 8.6.3?** No (`limit.rb` is absent in 8.6.3). It must ship in the same commit as the gem bump. - **Validation:** boot with production eager loading, check that `Pagy::DEFAULT.slice(:limit, :limit_param, :limit_max, :overflow)` returns 10, `:per_page`, 50, `:last_page`, and that `?limit=5` is ignored (probe rows `/notes?limit=5` and `/notes?items=5`). **R2. Rename the accessor in the view** (`app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30`) - **Change:** `@pagy.items` becomes `@pagy.limit`. - **When it applies:** always. On 9.3.5 every `/notes` render raises `undefined method 'items' for an instance of Pagy` (variant B). - **Works on 8.6.3?** No: 8.6.3 has no `Pagy#limit`, and a `respond_to?` shim isn't worth it. Ship it in the same commit. - **Validation:** `select[name=per_page] option[selected]` shows 5, 10, 25 or 50 for those sizes, 50 for `?per_page=500`, and nothing for `?per_page=7` (same as 8.6.3). **R3. Restore the page clamp** (`app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:18`) - **Why:** 8.6.3's `pagy_get_page` returned `[params[:page].to_i, 1].max`. In 9.3.5 it returns `(page || 1).to_i` with no clamp. In 9.0.0–9.0.2 it returned the raw parameter, and 9.0.3 changed it to the current form. I confirmed both by unpacking those gems. - **Effect:** `?page=` (blank), `0`, `-1` and `two` now raise `Pagy::VariableError: expected :page >= 1` (variant C). That is an `ArgumentError`, so production returns 500 for stale or hand-edited links. `ARCHITECTURE.md` promises page 1 for these. - **Change:** `@pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes, page: [params[:page].to_i, 1].max)`. Pagy uses an explicitly passed `page:` instead of reading the parameter, in both 8.x (`vars[:page] ||=`) and 9.x (`vars[:page] ||=`). An alternative is overriding `pagy_get_page(vars, **)` in the controller. Explicit `page:` is more local and doesn't depend on Pagy's private method names. - **Works on 8.6.3?** Yes, verified: full suite green and the probe matches the 8.6.3 baseline exactly. You can ship it ahead of the upgrade. - **Validation:** the existing test "invalid pages show the first page…" covers this. It fails on variant C and passes on D. **R4. Update the docs** (in the upgrade commit) - Change "Pagy 8.6.3" to "Pagy 9.3.5" in `ARCHITECTURE.md:17` and `docs/guides/controllers.md:108`. - `ARCHITECTURE.md:20-23` stays accurate: invalid pages still show page 1, and invalid `per_page` still raises `Pagy::VariableError`. ## Checked and unchanged (no action needed) - **`pagy_info` output:** byte-identical HTML (`Displaying notes 6-10 of 13 in total`, and "Displaying 25 notes" on a single page). The `pagy.info.*` keys and English strings are unchanged. The only locale-key rename (`items_selector_js` → `limit_selector_js`) is unused here. - **`pagy_url_for`:** same paths (it keeps `/journal`), same order of query parameters, filters preserved. 9.x moved `:fragment` and `:anchor_string` from Pagy variables to helper arguments, but the app uses neither. - **Overflow `:last_page`:** same result for `?page=99` and `?page=99&per_page=5`. The 9.0.8 change only affects `:empty_page`. - **Calling convention:** 9.x switched to keyword arguments (`pagy(collection, **vars)`). The app passes no vars today. The R3 call `pagy(@notes, page: …)` works on both versions. - **Size extra:** no longer auto-required in 9.x. The app doesn't use `series` or `pagy_nav`, so there's nothing to change. - **Ruby requirement:** `>= 3.1`, and the app runs 3.3.6. Rails 7.0.8.7 booted in production mode with eager loading, and `zeitwerk:check` passed. - **Behavior kept the same on purpose:** invalid `per_page` (blank, `0`, `-5`, `abc`) still raises `Pagy::VariableError`. Array or hash parameters (`page[]=2`, `per_page[]=5`, `page[a]=2`) still raise `NoMethodError` (500), on both versions and with R3. ## Not caught by the existing tests - **Error text and grouping:** for invalid `per_page`, the `VariableError` message and its `#variable` attribute change from `:items` to `:limit`. Nothing in the app rescues these, but any error-tracker grouping or alerting that matches on the message will see new groups. - **Other probed behaviors:** none of these have a test, but the probe showed them identical on both versions: `/journal` links, ignoring `?limit=` and `?items=`, the selected option for a size not in the list, and fractional or suffixed pages (`1.9` → page 1, `2abc` → page 2). - **Partial renames:** a partial R1 (for example renaming the parameter key but not `limit_max`) is caught by the existing tests (variant B2 failed). Fixing only the `require` plus the view fails "pages through…" because `per_page` is ignored. ## Optional (not required, not recommended in this upgrade) - **Version constraint:** upstream recommends `~> 9.3`. Keep the exact pin `"9.3.5"`, per the repo rule against changing dependency versions without authorization. - **Copying the 9.3.5 initializer template** (`config/pagy.rb` in the gem): not needed. The four explicit settings are clearer. - **Keyset pagination (new in 9.x):** not recommended. It would change the URL format (an encoded cursor instead of a page number), break bookmarks, and drop the totals shown in `pagy_info`. - **Handling invalid `per_page` and array parameters gracefully** (for example `params[:page].to_s.to_i`, or rescuing to defaults): this would change documented behavior, so it belongs in a separate, authorized change rather than this upgrade. - **Pagy 43.x** (the next major after 9) is a much larger rewrite and out of scope. ## Rollout, mixed versions and rollback - **Order:** 1. Optional: deploy R3 on 8.6.3 first. It's verified to change nothing there. 2. Deploy one commit with the Gemfile and lockfile bump, R1, R2 and R4. - **Never deploy the gem bump without R1 and R2.** Web and Sidekiq processes would fail to boot. - **Queued Sidekiq jobs:** if workers fail to boot, the jobs wait in Redis and are not lost. No job serializes Pagy objects or arguments, so jobs queued before the deploy run fine after it, and the same holds for rollback. - **Mixed fleet during a rolling deploy:** old and new processes produce identical URLs (`page`, `per_page`), identical HTML and identical links. A link rendered by a 9.3.5 process works on an 8.6.3 process and the other way round. With R3 deployed, invalid-page handling also matches. Without R3, 9.3.5 processes return 500 where 8.6.3 processes return page 1. - **Stored data and caches:** none affected. There is no database column, session key (the session holds only the user ID), Redis key or cached fragment that depends on pagination. - **Rollback:** revert the upgrade commit. R3 can stay, since it's valid on 8.6.3. There's no data to migrate back. ## Experiments run **Isolation.** All experiments ran in disposable copies, never the working app: - **Copies:** `git clone` into `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/v8` and `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/v9`. Each copy's `config/database.yml` was changed to use databases named `pagyexp__*` on the local Postgres 15 server. That's a separate database on a shared server, not a separate cluster. - **Redis:** a dedicated `redis-server --port 6391 --save ""`, with `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6391/0`. Its command stats show the digest tests' 18 `sadd` and 15 `srem` calls landed there. The shared 6379 instance shows no `sadd`/`srem` calls since it started. - **Gems:** pagy 9.3.5 went into an isolated `GEM_HOME=/tmp/pagy-upgrade/gems`, with the shared gem directory read-only on `GEM_PATH`. The shared gem directory still holds only pagy-8.6.3. - **Storage and cache:** storage was the copy's own `tmp/storage`. The test cache is `:null_store`. - **Environment file:** `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/env.sh`. - **Cleanup:** afterwards I dropped the `pagyexp_*` databases and shut down the 6391 Redis. Copies and logs are kept. - **Working app:** `/home/user/workspace/repo` has a clean `git status` at `9938031`. **Gem source:** `pagy-9.3.5.gem`, sha256 `78a95131…0fd7`. It, plus 9.0.0, 9.0.2 and 9.0.3 for attribution, is unpacked under `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/src/`. The changelog is at `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/dl/CHANGELOG-9.3.5.md`. **Variants** (commits in `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/v9`, each running pagy 9.3.5 from `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/gems/gems/pagy-9.3.5`): | Variant | Change | Command | Result | Log | |---|---|---|---|---| | v8 baseline (8.6.3) | none | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 0 failures | `logs/v8-baseline-test.log` | | A `85d1f8a` | Gemfile bump only | `RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:prepare` | `LoadError pagy/extras/items` | `logs/v9A-dbprepare.log` | | B `707dc52` | + rename `require` only | notes test | 6 errors: `undefined method 'items'` (×5), `VariableError page` | `logs/v9B-notes-test.log` | | B2 `0a83e57` | + view `limit`, old keys left | notes test | 1 failure (per_page ignored), 1 VariableError | `logs/v9B2-notes-test.log` | | C `80dd2ac` | full R1 + R2 | notes test | 1 error, `expected :page >= 1; got 0` | `logs/v9C-notes-test.log` | | D `153e2c7` | C + R3 | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 325 assertions, 0 failures | `logs/v9D-full-test.log` | | D | | `bin/rails zeitwerk:check` | All is good | `logs/v9D-zeitwerk.log` | | D | | production runner with `eager_load!` | 9.3.5, expected defaults | `logs/v9D-prod-boot.log` | | P8 `051c3d5` (v8 copy, 8.6.3) | R3 only | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 0 failures | `logs/v8P-full-test.log` | - **Full diff of the passing variant D:** `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/logs/v9D-final.diff`. - **Probe:** a disposable integration test, `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/probe/pagy_probe_test.rb`. It was copied into each copy only for the run and then deleted. It covers 26 URLs over 25 notes. - **Probe results:** per-variant JSON in `logs/probe-{v8baseline,v8prep,v9C,v9D}.json`, side by side in `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/logs/probe-comparison.txt`. - **What the probe shows:** v8 baseline, v8 with R3, and v9D match everywhere except the error text for invalid `per_page`. v9C additionally raises on the four invalid-page URLs. ## Checks still to run 1. In the real upgrade branch, rerun `bin/rails test` and the probe matrix, keeping the probe out of the repo, against D's diff. 2. Run a browser smoke test of `/notes` and `/journal`: change "Per page", go next and previous, and load `?page=0`. It isn't automated because `test/system` is empty. 3. Check how the error tracker groups `Pagy::VariableError` for `:limit` versus `:items`. 4. In staging, boot a Sidekiq worker on the new commit to confirm it starts. ## Unverified claims and open questions - Whether production has more than one process or host running at once (which would make a rolling mixed fleet real) is assumed, not observed. - I don't know whether any external client or monitoring depends on the `VariableError` message text. - I checked only the en locale. The app sets no other locale, so Pagy's other locales are irrelevant unless one is added. - The 9.x page-clamp removal is inferred from source diffs. It isn't in the changelog and I didn't look for an upstream issue. --- ## Notes on the plan - **Experiment isolation:** the disposable copies used their own databases on the shared local Postgres server, not a separate Postgres cluster. Redis and gem installs were fully isolated. The `pagyexp_*` databases were dropped afterwards. - **The page clamp (R3) needs the most attention.** It isn't in the upstream changelog, and the upgrade fails without it even after the renames. Without it, invalid page values return a 500 instead of page 1. The existing test "invalid pages show the first page…" catches it, but only if you run the suite. Shipping R3 on 8.6.3 first is low-risk because it changes nothing there. - **Evidence:** the copies, logs and passing diff are under `/tmp/pagy-upgrade/`.
